instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Failure Reveals the Mission
cards.instruction: Use each failed step to reveal a different goal the plan was secretly pursuing, then act immediately on that new mission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three knocks, same as you. Treasure hunters' greeting. The map's brought us to wake this wall; I'll knock louder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking whether it's hollow. Solid. And our torch is nearly out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Solid, yes. We were sent to hear it in darkness. I'll put the torch out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can only hear you breathing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The map was testing our breath control. I'm holding mine; listen now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tapped the radio like you. Report sent. Base hasn't answered; we were sent to listen. I'll try another channel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was knocking water out. That's only static; I need a forecast before my watch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Water cleared, yes. That's applause. Our mission is entertaining base. I'll sing our report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now there's silence. Even the static's stopped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This was rejection training. Tell me you won't hear a second verse; I'll ask again.

cards.title: Fluent in Nonsense
cards.instruction: Perform complete mastery of the strange logic while inventing each rule only when it becomes necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've held my tape up like yours. Third elbow, obviously. We can price this bottled cloud once you measure it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was measuring shelf space. The cloud only has two elbows.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shelves first, yes. Its third elbow appears when you address it as Professor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Professor. It's raining inside the bottle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Its credentials. Count the drops; a pound per qualification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've bowed like you. Respect first. Now turn the gravity dial politely and we'll get your sofa off the ceiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was ducking under it. I'm losing my deposit; how do I turn politely?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Head safely lowered, yes. Pause at each number. They dislike being passed over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six clicked, but now the armchairs are rising.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six has invited witnesses. Apologise where all the chairs can hear you.

cards.title: Raise the Impossibility
cards.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've raised my hand too. Table for two in the air. Your flying chair needs a flying table; dinner should travel with the diner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking ceiling height. I can make the table circle the room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Height checked. Add a hovering waiter; nobody should chase their soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter can serve while flying upside down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then commission gravity-proof soup. I won't make customers rotate between courses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I left blank names beside yours. Invisible companions, naturally. I'll give your invisible wedding guest a whole table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hadn't asked her name. Her family walks through walls; they tend to wander.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Names later. I'll rent a ballroom that follows them. Nobody should miss cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our ballroom can split itself when guests wander apart.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll order a cake that multiplies with it. Every room deserves the first slice.

cards.title: Every Glitch Is a Gift
cards.instruction: Turn every contradiction or failure into a surprising benefit of the impossible system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two turns, like you. Picnic setting. The garden door's opened into the broom cupboard; take a brush for the crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The key was sticking. Now it's the attic. I'm carrying all the sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lock freed. Grab the picnic blanket without climbing stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's the cellar. The sandwiches are getting warm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Built-in refrigeration. Put them beside the wine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned the office clock back like your watch. Office time. It's taken us back to the meeting we missed; we can still attend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch was fast. This is too far back; I haven't received the invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clocks corrected. Extra preparation time; let's get our notes ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's before the booking. The boss is asking me whether we need this meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Tell her no; we can keep that afternoon free.

cards.title: Calm About the Impossible
cards.instruction: Remain perfectly calm around impossible events while becoming increasingly alarmed by ordinary details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I cupped my hands round my mouth like you. Dragon greetings. He can stay for tea; do wipe those biscuit crumbs off my carpet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was calling him back. His three heads breathe fire; should I take him outside?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Called in, yes. He's fine. Three mouths? I need three napkins immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought his own. They're paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paper? At my good table? Fetch the linen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I whistled like you. Up it goes. The table can float while we pack, but put a mat under that wet cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was calling the cat. The table's at the ceiling; I'll pull it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cat called, yes. Wait! You'll slide the cup across the polish. Use the stepladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll climb up. I've still got my muddy boots on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Boots off! You'll grind mud into every tread.
